name: Hawaii Tourism Length-of-Stay Analysis Project
what_it_holds: Committed raw file 'Hawaii Tourism Data (from DBEDT Data Warehouse) (1).csv' (Hawaii Dept. of Business, Economic Development & Tourism data warehouse export), 1999-2021, broken out by visitor category (air, hotel-only, etc.) and island. Repo also has HawaiiLOS.sql (analysis queries) and derived Excel outputs: avg_los.xlsx, first_time_los.xlsx, repeat_los.xlsx, first_time_repeat_los_yearly.xlsx, YoY_visitors.xlsx, YoY_islands.xlsx — i.e. average length-of-stay split by first-time vs. repeat visitor, by year and by island. References a companion Kaggle dataset 'hawaii-travel-length-of-trip'.
why_useful: We already hold Hawaii DBEDT visitor stats as 'the only public party-size series' — this repo's committed CSV covers a longer span (1999-2021 vs whatever vintage we pulled) and, more importantly, has length-of-stay decomposed by first-time vs. repeat visitor and by island, which is new granularity directly on gap #20 (length-of-stay / party-size proxies) and is a Hawaii-like template that could be replicated for other STR-heavy island destinations.
size_hint: one CSV + several small xlsx outputs
duplicate_of_holding: Hawaii DBEDT visitor stats (partial overlap) - this version is longer-history and has first-time/repeat LOS splits we don't currently have
themes: Caribbean, Central America and island tourism stats (CTO, Costa Rica ICT, Dominican Republic BCRD, Bahamas, Puerto Rico) and Hawaii-like party-size / length-of-stay surveys
why_all: We already hold Hawaii DBEDT visitor stats as 'the only public party-size series' — this repo's committed CSV covers a longer span (1999-2021 vs whatever vintage we pulled) and, more importantly, has length-of-stay decomposed by first-time vs. repeat visitor and by island, which is new granularity directly on gap #20 (length-of-stay / party-size proxies) and is a Hawaii-like template that could be replicated for other STR-heavy island destinations.

name: IPS-mlops
what_it_holds: Committed file ips_2023.csv: UK Office for National Statistics International Passenger Survey (IPS) 2023 microdata, 252,260 individual overseas-visitor-to-UK records, 61 variables including trip purpose, duration/length of stay, nationality, destination country/region within UK, transport mode, package vs independent travel, fare class, and total expenditure (target variable for the repo's ML pipeline). Also includes process.ipynb/process.html (EDA + feature engineering + model training) and requirements.txt. Single calendar year (2023) only, one-off ONS release rather than a maintained pull.
why_useful: Confirms IPS 2023 microdata exists at UK Data Service with row-level trip records (trip purpose, party info typically included in IPS schema); repo's pipeline code shows which fields matter and gives a working ETL to adapt if UKDS access is obtained.
themes: Length-of-stay, party-size and trip-purpose survey microdata (NTTO SIAT, UK IPS, Eurostat tour_dem, Japan travel survey, national travel surveys)
why_all: Confirms IPS 2023 microdata exists at UK Data Service with row-level trip records (trip purpose, party info typically included in IPS schema); repo's pipeline code shows which fields matter and gives a working ETL to adapt if UKDS access is obtained.

Directly addresses gap #20 (party size / length-of-stay / trip-purpose survey microdata) via one of the exact named source families (UK IPS) with a genuinely committed row-level CSV, not just a pointer -- unusually granular (61 fields, quarter-of-century-old survey vintage that predates most alt-data digitization). Length-of-stay and purpose-of-visit distributions for UK inbound travel are a plausible cross-check for STR demand mix (leisure vs business) in the EMEA region ABNB reports.

name: TFL_Stations
what_it_holds: Committed `/data` folder of TfL station entry/exit CSVs by time-of-day and day-of-week, sourced from the TfL Open Data portal's annual station-usage releases; figures pre-2017 cover London Underground only, 2017+ covers the wider TfL network (rail, tram, DLR). Includes a compiled `Stations_20220221.csv` master station list. Processed outputs (CSV, maps, images) also committed under `/output`.
why_useful: Station-level London ridership 2007-2021 including Heathrow Express/Piccadilly line stations at Heathrow terminals — a usable airport-rail-linked visitor proxy for London, ABNB's largest EMEA/UK market, and a long historical panel (14 years) versus most repos here.
license: none stated (derived from TfL Open Data, non-commercial TfL licence terms apply to source)
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: Station-level London ridership 2007-2021 including Heathrow Express/Piccadilly line stations at Heathrow terminals — a usable airport-rail-linked visitor proxy for London, ABNB's largest EMEA/UK market, and a long historical panel (14 years) versus most repos here.

name: flight-price-prediction (Kayak scraper)
what_it_holds: CSV of 55,363 rows x 7 columns committed in /data: source/destination airport (4 sources, 4 destinations), number of stops, airline, average price by airline, flight duration, and ticket price, scraped from Kayak via an included scraper notebook. Random-forest price-prediction model on top. Years/specific city pairs not stated in the README.
why_useful: A working, actively-maintained (updated 2026-09-08) non-Airbnb scraper for flight prices could be repurposed as a cheap, point-in-time-capable proxy for travel-demand/price intensity feeding gap 10 (airline/transport capacity) and cross-checking consumer travel-spend strength; scraping Kayak is not on the sanctioned-source list, so running it is a ToS decision for a human, not something to execute here.
time_coverage: point-in-time scrape at run time; historical scraped sample committed in repo (date range not specified in listing)
size_hint: small scraped CSV sample plus scraper script (~repo is a few hundred KB)
themes: Expedia and Hotels.com datasets (Expedia hotel recommendation Kaggle, personalized ranking ICDM 2013, Expedia scrapers), Trivago RecSys 2019, Kayak/Skyscanner scrapers
Google Hotel Ads / Google Travel price datasets and scrapers; hotel metasearch price panels
Kaggle competitions and datasets on travel demand forecasting mirrored on GitHub (Expedia, Trivago, Booking, Airbnb new-user bookings, hotel demand)
why_all: A working, actively-maintained (updated 2026-09-08) non-Airbnb scraper for flight prices could be repurposed as a cheap, point-in-time-capable proxy for travel-demand/price intensity feeding gap 10 (airline/transport capacity) and cross-checking consumer travel-spend strength; scraping Kayak is not on the sanctioned-source list, so running it is a ToS decision for a human, not something to execute here.

Committed flight-price dataset scraped from Kayak could serve as a low-value cross-check on general travel-price/demand trends (peripheral to ABNB, closer to airline capacity gap #10), but scope and vintage are almost certainly narrow (single-route/date snapshot typical of these portfolio projects) -- worth a look only if airline-fare read-through becomes a workstream.

Not hotel metasearch, but the only repo in this whole sweep that pairs a committed scraped dataset with a working, currently-referenced metasearch-style scraper (Kayak) — a template for what a hotel-price panel repo would need to look like (none found). Marginal fit to this theme; flagged as the closest structural analogue.

A small but real, self-collected (not a stale Kaggle mirror) airfare pricing dataset -- a possible airline-capacity/pricing proxy for gap #10 (airline capacity and traffic) and a demonstrated working Kayak-scraping method that could be pointed at other routes if a human signs off on scraping Kayak.

name: siloah-travel-mcp
what_it_holds: MCP server + REST API (mcp.siloah.travel) indexing 70,000+ cruise voyages, 678 ships, 62 cruise lines (20 active), 6,700+ ports, 11,000+ cabin types across 30 languages. No local data files committed — queries a live Postgres/Supabase+pgvector backend on Cloudflare Workers; supports filtering by destination, departure city, cruise line, duration, price. MIT licensed, 7 commits.
why_useful: A single free API surface that already aggregates cruise-line schedule/capacity breadth (ships, itineraries, ports) across 62 lines including NCLH/RCL/CCL brands — could be pulled repeatedly to build a point-in-time itinerary-count/capacity proxy for gap #18 (cruise book-ahead analogue) without scraping individual cruise-line sites.
time_coverage: current/live snapshot only (no historical vintages found)
size_hint: 70k voyages, 678 ships, 6.7k ports (live DB, not committed)
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: A single free API surface that already aggregates cruise-line schedule/capacity breadth (ships, itineraries, ports) across 62 lines including NCLH/RCL/CCL brands — could be pulled repeatedly to build a point-in-time itinerary-count/capacity proxy for gap #18 (cruise book-ahead analogue) without scraping individual cruise-line sites.
